segments.text: This is a live engine. Every point is a word it knows. Every line is a connection it has made for itself. Two research projects run on it: Neuron, and Cortex.
Neuron. Ask it to define a word it has never been given.
It reads its sources, and works the word into the graph, along with every word it met on the way. Twenty-nine runs. Thirteen new words. Two seconds.
One typed line, and a tree of runs underneath it: the engine asking its own questions, and answering them.
Ask the same thing again, and nothing runs. It already knows. Learning happens once, and takes its time. Recall is immediate.
It can be told, and it can be changed, in a single line.
Every run leaves a receipt: the path it took through the graph. Any run can be played back, hop by hop.
Cortex. The same engine, holding a project: its scope, its checkpoints, what is expected, and where things stand.

Each session reports what it did, as a line. Say a thing twice, and it is not stored twice. It is the same memory, with a new time. The next session starts from the state of the work, not from a transcript.
Cortex and Neuron. Research and engineering by James Huson. Find both at exnulla dot com.
